title: Filtration, turnover and automatic dosing requirements
audience: Pool service technicians and operators who check filtration and automatic dosing at public pools in SA. Electrical work on pumps, controllers and dosing equipment is licensed where it applies. Figures apply under the state standard.
learningOutcomes: State the turnover limits for each pool type in the South Australian standard.
Calculate the flow needed to meet a turnover limit for a given pool volume.
Explain what auto-dosing and sensing must do, and what a worker must still check manually.

instruction.heading: Continuous circulation through the filter
instruction.body: Each public pool and spa needs a filter system that keeps water moving through it non-stop. Enough water has to run through the filter to keep it clean and clear. That is measured as turnover: the time needed to cycle a volume equal to the entire basin through the filter media. Turnover is a condition for every pool type the standard covers, not an optional extra.

instruction.heading: Turnover limits by pool type
instruction.body: A swimming pool needs its whole volume filtered no less often than every six hours. A wading pool needs it no less often than every two hours. A waterslide pool needs it no less often than hourly. A spa needs its volume cycled at least every half hour. Hydrotherapy water needs its volume cycled no less often than every two hours, with under an hour suggested for busy pools, for example ones running fitness classes. Where requirements vary, a separate filter is recommended.

instruction.heading: Filter types and hydrotherapy pools
instruction.body: The standard calls a sand filter one that uses sand and gravel media. For hydrotherapy pools it says a dedicated filtration system is ideal, and it does not recommend cartridge units or diatomaceous earth types for them. Backwashing reverses water flow to clean the filter, and it removes water and disinfectant, so follow the operator plan for timing and for managing the discharge.

instruction.heading: Auto-dosing and sensing
instruction.body: Each pool must have auto-dosing and sensing equipment that watches and corrects the pH and sanitiser level around the clock, keeping them in the ranges set by the standard's tables. The equipment does not remove the need to test. Check its readings against a manual test, know what its alarms mean, and escalate any fault. Repair, wiring and controller work is licensed where a licence applies.

instruction.heading: Working out the flow needed
instruction.body: To check turnover, divide the pool volume in litres by the minutes allowed for turnover to get the minimum flow in L/min. For example, a 300,000 litre swimming pool with a six-hour limit needs about 830 L/min through the filter. Verify that the pump, filter and pipework can deliver that flow, and that the flow is not reduced by a dirty filter.

procedure: Confirm the pool type and its turnover limit from the standard's rules.
Measure or read the pump flow and filter pressure, and calculate the turnover achieved.
Compare the achieved turnover with the limit and record the result.
Test pH and disinfectant manually, and compare them with the automatic dosing readings.
Isolate electrical supply before any inspection of pumps or controllers, and escalate any fault to a licensed electrician where required.

workedExamples.situation: A public pool holds 300,000 litres. The pump reads 600 L/min.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Does the pool meet the swimming pool turnover limit?
workedExamples.reasoning: At 600 L/min, 300,000 litres takes 500 minutes, which is about 8.3 hours. The swimming pool limit is six hours, so the turnover is too slow. Escalate to the operator, check the filter for blockage and the pump for wear, and do not treat the pool as compliant until the flow is increased.

equipmentAndPpe: Flow meter or pump data sheet
Pressure gauge reading for the filter
Calibrated pH and disinfectant test kit
Insulated tools and lock-out device for electrical isolation

commonErrors.error: Trusting the dosing controller and skipping the manual test.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the controller reading against a manual test, and record both.

commonErrors.error: Reducing pump speed to save power and breaking the turnover limit.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the turnover after any change to pump speed.

commonErrors.error: Ignoring a dirty filter that slows flow.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the pressure reading, and clean or service the filter as the plan sets.

commonErrors.error: Opening electrical enclosures without isolating the supply.
commonErrors.prevention: Isolate and lock out before any electrical work, and leave repairs to licensed electricians.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electricity and water are a fatal combination. Isolate supply before inspection, keep the pump area dry, and do not work on live equipment.
Repair, wiring and controller work on pool dosing and filtration equipment is licensed where a licence applies. This lesson does not grant a licence.
Backwash water and anything discharged from the pool may fall under rules set by the water authority or council. Check before discharge.
Figures are South Australian standard values (revised 2013). Confirm the current regulation text.

qualityStandard: Achieved turnover is recorded and compared against the limit for the pool type.
Automatic dosing readings are verified against a manual test at each check.
Electrical isolation is recorded before any inspection of pumps or controllers.
documentationEvidence: Turnover calculation record with volume, flow, time and result
Automatic dosing verification record with manual test comparison
Electrical isolation record and licensed-repair referral where needed
summary: Turnover limits: swimming pool 6 hours, wading 2 hours, waterslide 1 hour, spa 30 minutes, hydrotherapy 2 hours (under 1 hour recommended for heavy use).
Automatic dosing must run continuously, and manual tests still verify it.
Isolate electrical supply, and leave wiring and controller repairs to licensed people.

options: Yes, if the equipment is new
